runtime_implementation.target: Standalone Rust OM9; Windows x64; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=H:/OpenMatrix9/cargo-target; -j 2; app tests need the OCCT bin and VC runtime on PATH
runtime_implementation.scope: Typed gem instance edit/report owner: partial attribute edits, mask-based Match Attributes, a versioned gem style store, geometry regeneration from the stored record, numbered map rows, count/weight aggregation and an attribute history that keeps the GemId and the om9.gem.placement link
runtime_implementation.notes: Sửa gem là dữ liệu thuần rồi commit một transaction; GemId, object id và link om9.gem.placement được giữ qua mọi lần sửa. Style ghi atomic vào store có version. Reporter dùng volume lưới × density theo bảng vật liệu và đối chiếu công thức thương mại ±15%, in rõ 'NOT A CERTIFICATE'. Gem Map có overlay đánh số trong viewport kèm cửa sổ key. 9 L3 đều còn gate M05-UI.
remaining: All nine L3 keep the M05-UI manual gate open: no human has reviewed the edit/report commands on screen and no reviewer signature is claimed.
Only Windows x64 was exercised in this run.
The app test binaries link OCCT, so the run needs the OCCT bin and VC runtime directories on PATH; that environment requirement is recorded, not hidden.
CARGO_TARGET_DIR is H:/OpenMatrix9/cargo-target because this sandbox denies writes to the L:/om9-target directory named in AGENTS.md.

The clippy gate runs with `--cap-lints warn` and is scoped to the files this task owns: the shared checkout also contains concurrent in-flight work whose deny-by-default clippy error (settings/bezel.rs) would otherwise stop the whole batch; those diagnostics are listed in clippy_foreign_warnings.

The Gem Map overlay is automated-tested as projection data (one numbered caption per visible stone, captions clamped inside the viewport, off-screen stones skipped) and is painted in the committed viewport path; human pixel acceptance still needs the M05-UI pass.

The reporter's mass is the closed mesh volume × the material density from the gemological table, cross-checked against the published trade formula inside a ±15% band; it stays a computed value and the report prints `NOT A CERTIFICATE`, because only a gemologist can certify a stone.
